nodes.name: Increase Global Equities Execution Market Share
Scale AI-Augmented Research Coverage to Top-4 Peer Parity
Reduce Algo Execution Implementation Shortfall Below Peer Median
Grow Prime Brokerage Client Balances in APAC & EMEA
Consolidate Onto a Single Global Order & Execution Management Platform
nodes.rationale: Citi Equities runs order and execution management on a patchwork of legacy, region-specific systems (including the Direct Market Access gateway) that fragments execution-quality data and slows every attempt to standardise algo strategies globally.
nodes.options_considered: Retain the regional OMS/EMS patchwork and integrate at the edges; build a new platform from scratch; buy a leading third-party OEMS; consolidate onto the existing Velocity platform globally
nodes.chosen_option: Consolidate globally onto the existing Velocity OEMS platform — fastest path to a single execution-quality dataset without a multi-year rebuild
nodes.consequences: Easier: one global view of execution quality and market share, faster algo strategy rollout, lower run cost from retiring the DMA gateway. Harder: a multi-region migration with real cutover risk, and short-term disruption to APAC desks still on the legacy gateway.

nodes.name: Migrate Market Data & Tick Store to a Cloud-Native Platform
nodes.rationale: The current on-prem tick store is approaching end-of-life, can't elastically scale for new alternative-data ingestion, and is a named single point of failure for every downstream trading and research system.
nodes.options_considered: Refresh the on-prem hardware in place; move to a managed on-prem alternative; migrate to a cloud-native tick store and messaging platform; build a hybrid model
nodes.chosen_option: Migrate to a cloud-native tick store and messaging platform, keeping only latency-critical matching-adjacent components co-located
nodes.consequences: Easier: elastic scaling for new data sources, reduced patching/DR burden, a single golden source feeding both trading and AI research pipelines. Harder: recurring cloud cost replaces one-off capital spend, and low-latency paths need careful re-architecture to avoid execution-quality regressions.

nodes.name: Establish Central AI Model Risk Governance for Trading & Research Models
nodes.rationale: Three AI models are now in flight across execution and research with no single governance gate — a regulator or internal audit finding here could stall the whole AI-augmented transformation programme, not just one model.
nodes.options_considered: Leave governance decentralised within each desk; adopt an existing enterprise-wide model risk framework unmodified; stand up a dedicated Equities AI Model Governance Committee with its own sign-off gate
nodes.chosen_option: Not yet finalised — proposed, pending review
nodes.consequences: Easier (anticipated): one consistent explainability and human-oversight bar before any AI model reaches production, faster regulator conversations. Harder (anticipated): an additional sign-off step in the model delivery pipeline, and desks used to moving fast will feel the friction first.

nodes.description: Wanted to push AI-generated research summaries direct to retail-adjacent channels; compliance couldn't clear direct-to-retail distribution of AI-generated content without an explainability and licensing rework, so it was shelved.

nodes.name: Cross-Asset Sentiment Trading Signal Pilot
nodes.description: Wanted to pilot a cross-asset alt-data sentiment signal; the legacy tick store couldn't ingest new alternative-data feeds fast enough to make the signal usable intraday, so the pilot never left the lab.

nodes.name: Real-Time Cross-Venue Liquidity Heatmap
nodes.description: Wanted a real-time cross-venue liquidity heatmap for the trading desk; the OMS couldn't stream order-book data in real time without a rearchitecture, so it shipped as a 15-minute-delayed view the desk still finds too slow to act on.

nodes.name: Research Coverage Breadth Matched to Top-4 Peers
Sub-Millisecond Smart Order Router Latency
nodes.acceptance_criteria: Order routing decisions complete in under 1ms at the 99th percentile across all connected venues
nodes.rationale: Top-4 peers already route sub-millisecond; every extra millisecond of router latency measurably widens implementation shortfall on liquid names

nodes.name: Co-Located Matching Engine Access in Key Venues
nodes.acceptance_criteria: Order flow for the top 10 venues by volume is co-located, verified by round-trip latency audit
nodes.rationale: Sub-millisecond routing is unreachable without co-location for the venues that carry the majority of volume

nodes.name: Explainable AI Signals for Research Distribution
nodes.acceptance_criteria: Every AI-generated research signal ships with a human-readable rationale a PM can audit before acting on it
nodes.rationale: Portfolio managers and compliance won't act on — or clear — a signal they can't explain, no matter how accurate it is

nodes.name: Single Golden Source Market & Reference Data
nodes.acceptance_criteria: Every trading, research and risk system reads market/reference data from one platform, with zero reconciliation breaks in a week
nodes.rationale: Trading, research and risk currently reconcile against slightly different copies of reference data, producing intermittent, hard-to-diagnose discrepancies

nodes.name: Real-Time Cross-Venue Best Execution Reporting
nodes.acceptance_criteria: Execution-quality reporting is available to the desk within 60 seconds of a fill, across every connected venue
nodes.rationale: Best-execution reporting is currently a T+1 batch job, so the desk can't adjust algo behaviour intraday when execution quality is slipping

nodes.name: Model Risk Sign-Off Prior to Production AI Deployment
nodes.acceptance_criteria: No AI model reaches production trading or client-facing research without a documented model-risk sign-off
nodes.rationale: An unreviewed model making live trading or client-facing decisions is an unacceptable regulatory and reputational exposure
